releases.title: Cloudhunter
releases.label: Better Company
releases.why: KEXP's music directors reviewed the Portland songwriter's new EP in their Oct. 19 New Music Reviews for DJs, calling it a beautiful set of evocative indie folk.

releases.title: Doggone
releases.label: Full Time Hobby
releases.why: Third full-length, recorded in Portland with Rose City Band's Rick Pedrosa and guests Devendra Banhart and Merle Law; The Line of Best Fit gave it 8/10 and it led the Mercury's Oct. 23 Spin Cycle.

releases.title: Daniel Loves Mandy Forever
releases.why: Willamette Week profiled the Portland band's slightly stripped-back follow-up to its shoegaze-leaning records on Oct. 14.

releases.title: There Is No Evil
releases.why: The Portland shoegaze band's second album, written around frontman Krinsky's North Portland house by I-5; Willamette Week profiled it ahead of the Oct. 22 Show Bar release show.

releases.title: Sympathy for the Decibel
releases.label: Sonic Jett Records
releases.why: New EP from the Portland punk lifers, following 2023's Under the Dagger and 2025's The Monkey's Paw; covered by MHF Magazine.

releases.title: Abaraz
releases.why: The Portland ensemble's new album, inspired by a residency at an oasis on the edge of the Sahara; featured on OPB's Think Out Loud.

releases.title: Linda's Head
releases.label: Kranky
releases.why: First album in over a decade from the trio with Liz Harris (Grouper); covered by Willamette Week, Stereogum ("sounds spectacular"), Flood and Spectrum Culture (84%).

releases.title: Offerings for Weary Dogs
releases.why: The Portland quartet's second album, reviewed by the Portland Mercury, which says the band swaps "or" for "and" and dissolves binaries.

releases.title: Ave Trujillo
releases.label: El Cortez Records
releases.why: Fifth solo album from the Richmond Fontaine and Delines bassist, with each song named for a bird; featured on OPB's Think Out Loud.

releases.title: Furthermore
releases.label: Jealous Butcher Records
releases.why: The Portland queercore band's first album in 30 years, announced via Stereogum and covered by BrooklynVegan and The Line of Best Fit.

releases.title: Under Crushing Rain
releases.label: Static Catsup Aspic
releases.why: Hutch Harris's first Thermals album in a decade, a lo-fi throwback to the early records; announced via BrooklynVegan with lead single "Spirit Collectors".

releases.title: Shadow Work
releases.label: PJCE Records
releases.why: An 18-musician suite from Portland's jazz, classical and indie scenes, produced by Todd Sickafoose; on Willamette Week's fall must-hear list and profiled there.

releases.title: Temple Songs
releases.label: Raven Marching Band Records
releases.why: Her 14th solo album, recorded almost entirely alone in her backyard studio; reviewed by Willamette Week.

releases.title: do you love the color of the sky?
releases.label: Polyvinyl
releases.why: The band's third album and Polyvinyl debut, reviewed for airplay in KEXP's Oct. 19 New Music Reviews.

releases.title: I See Them, I See Me
releases.label: Double Double Whammy
releases.why: No. 1 on KVSC's college radio Top 30 for the week of Oct. 6 and named as a challenger at the top of the NACC chart; announced via Stereogum.

releases.title: Nature's Pill
releases.label: Winspear
releases.why: The Indianapolis band's second album was No. 2 on KVSC's college radio Top 30 for the week of Oct. 6 and is pushing for the top of the NACC chart.

releases.title: Pylon
releases.label: Dirty Hit
releases.why: No. 1 on the NACC college radio chart for the week of Oct. 14, her second album to top it for more than a week; The Crimson gave it 4 stars.

releases.title: Cancel Me (I'm Tired)
releases.label: Domino
releases.why: The London seven-piece's second album, reviewed for rotation in KEXP's Oct. 5 New Music Reviews and on KEXP's chart.

releases.title: Uncle
releases.label: K Records
releases.why: Fifth album from Ben Funkhouser's project, a guitar-forward alt-rock record produced by Alex Farrar, reviewed for airplay in KEXP's Oct. 19 New Music Reviews.

releases.title: All Set The Bone
releases.label: Transgressive/Canvasback
releases.why: KEXP's music directors called it an arresting set of rock-forward alt-country in their Oct. 5 New Music Reviews.
